In the United States, five states do not impose a statewide sales tax: Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon [d1][d2][d3][d5][d9]. These states are sometimes collectively referred to as the "NOMAD" states [d2][d8]. However, residents and businesses should be aware that some of these states allow local jurisdictions to levy their own sales taxes—Alaska, for example, has more than 100 local municipalities that impose local sales taxes [d1][d2][d3]. Additionally, all five states may still impose other types of taxes such as excise taxes, gross receipts taxes (Delaware), or income taxes (Oregon), so the absence of a statewide sales tax does not mean a completely tax-free environment [d2][d3][d8].
